newsitem.title: USA: Exiled Rwandan king calls for end to fighting.
newsitem.headline: Exiled Rwandan king calls for end to fighting.

text.p: Rwanda's exiled King Kigeli V issued a statement on Saturday appealing for an end to bitter fighting in eastern Zaire.

"This is an appeal to both governments of Zaire and Rwanda, requesting them to stop fighting, (sit) down and discuss ... their differences," Kigeli Ndahindurwa, who fled his country and took up residence in the United States in 1961, said in a statement from his home in a Washington suburb.
The fighting pits Zaire's army and allied Rwandan Hutu fighters against well-armed Tutsi rebels in the eastern provinces of North and South Kivu facing Rwanda and Burundi.
The United States has so far made ineffectual efforts to persuade Zairean and Rwandan leaders to talk to each other, but had said the diplomatic lead must come from the United Nations.

"Zairean and Rwandese people have been not only good friends for a long time, but really brothers, sharing the colonial experiences and the struggle to achieve independence of their two countries," Kigeli said.
"It (would) be a shame to spoil that brotherhood, instead of using our African traditional way of sitting down, (discussing) the matter and (finding) a good solution," he said.

Fighting in eastern Zaire dislodged more than 500,000 refugees from Rwanda's and Burundi's civil wars. Warfare between Zairean-born Tutsis, known as Banjamulenge, and other local tribes has led to an exodus of Rwandan Hutu refugees who fled to Zaire in the summer of 1994. Both the Zairean and Rwandan armies have entered the fray.
"You will never find peace with guns," Kigeli said. "You will only be killing your innocent brothers and sisters, and destroying your properties."
